chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:

Regarding a man who was fasting for ẓihār in Sha'ban and then the month of Ramadan came upon him, he said: “He fasts the month of Ramadan, then resumes the fasting. And if he had fasted in the ẓihār fast and exceeded the halfway point by a day, he completes its remainder.”

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: fasting, here referring to the expiatory fast
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: the halfway point of the required fasting period
key_terms.بَقِيَّتَهُ: its remainder; the rest of the fasting days to be completed
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose fasting takes precedence
key_terms.ظِهَارٍ: ẓihār; the pre-Islamic form of unlawful spousal declaration requiring expiation

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if fasting for the expiation of ẓihār is interrupted by Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about someone fasting an expiation for ẓihār when Ramadan begins. He must first fast Ramadan, then resume the expiation fast, unless he had already passed the midpoint of the expiatory fasting, in which case he completes what remains.
